trajectory.thought: The leader is a seeded baseline (mean on pool3) and the verdict is 'indistinguishable' — the runner-up is not statistically better. With only 3 validation windows, weight estimation is high-variance (as confirmed by the terrible a10 result), and the top 8 models are all within ~4% of each other. The mean over the 9 most stable models is a robust choice for this strongly trend-dominated, non-stationary series where no single model clearly dominates.

action_args.justification: The series is strongly trend-dominated (trend strength 0.97) with negligible seasonality (0.02) and is non-stationary. The top 8 models are tightly clustered (39.2–41.9 RMSE) with high error correlation (mean 0.74) and only moderate ranking stability (Kendall tau 0.48). With just 3 validation windows, fitted weights are high-variance (confirmed by the catastrophic a10 result). The mean over the 9 most consistently-ranked models (pool3) is a robust, low-variance combination that avoids the tail risk of the full pool (where the worst model has 1738 RMSE) while still benefiting from the diversity of the top cluster. The leader is a seed and the verdict is 'indistinguishable', so accepting is the correct call.

- Ranking stability is moderate (Kendall tau 0.478)
- Error correlation is high (mean 0.741), with 8 groups and only 4 independent
- The top models are all within ~4% of each other (39.16 to 41.89)
- The "rest" of models have much higher errors (median 58.45, worst 1737.8)
- The weighted strategy (a10) performed terribly (score 0.4425) - likely because with only 3 windows, weight estimation is high variance
- The plain mean of full pool (a1) also performed poorly (0.6833) - dragged down by bad models
- The DBA (a3) was worst (0.7048)

"If the leader is a SEED and the verdict is 'indistinguishable', accept it. The runner-up is not statistically better and more turns rarely turn noise into a real gain."

- The series is trend-dominated with high predictability
- The top 8 models are all within ~4% of each other
- There are redundant groups - many models are correlated
- The weighted approach failed badly (high variance with 3 windows)
- The mean of pool3 (9 models) is the best so far
